entries.name: VectorSpaceFiniteIffNoetherian
entries.binders: {k V : Type*} [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
entries.conclusion: Module.Finite k V ↔ IsNoetherian k V
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a ring or module through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: `k = V = ℚ`.

entries.name: VectorSpaceFiniteIffArtinian
entries.binders: {k V : Type*} [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]

entries.input: Let $k \geq 2$ and $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^k$. There is $\mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^k$ with $\mathbf{y} \neq \mathbf{0}$ and $\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y} = 0$.
entries.name: OrthogonalVectorExists
entries.binders: (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
entries.conclusion: ∃ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), y ≠ 0 ∧ inner ℝ x y = 0

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, $a \in K$ and $v \in V$. If $av = 0$, then $a = 0$ or $v = 0$.
entries.name: SmulEqZeroImpliesFactorZero
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (a : K) (v : V) (h : a • v = 0)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $K = V = \mathbb{Q}$, $a = 0$, $v = 1$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ and let $(U_i)_{i \in I}$ be any family of subspaces of $V$. Then the intersection $\bigcap_i U_i$ is a subspace of $V$: there is a subspace whose underlying set is exactly that intersection.
entries.name: SubspaceIntersectionIsSubspace
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {ι : Type*} (U : ι → Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: ∃ W : Submodule K V, (W : Set V) = ⋂ i, (U i : Set V)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the empty family in $\mathbb{Q}$, where the intersection is all of $V$.

entries.input: Let $U_1, U_2$ be subspaces of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. The union $U_1 \cup U_2$ is a subspace of $V$ (that is, it is the underlying set of some subspace) if and only if $U_1 \subseteq U_2$ or $U_2 \subseteq U_1$.
entries.name: UnionOfSubspacesIsSubspaceIff
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (U₁ U₂ : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: (∃ W : Submodule K V, (W : Set V) = (U₁ : Set V) ∪ U₂) ↔ U₁ ≤ U₂ ∨ U₂ ≤ U₁
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}^2$ with $U_1 = 0$, $U_2 = V$.

entries.input: Let $U_1, U_2$ be subspaces of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. The union $U_1 \cup U_2$ is a subspace of $V$ if and only if $U_1 \cap U_2 = 0$.
entries.name: UnionOfSubspacesIsSubspaceIffTwin
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (U₁ U₂ : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: (∃ W : Submodule K V, (W : Set V) = (U₁ : Set V) ∪ U₂) ↔ U₁ ⊓ U₂ = ⊥
entries.rationale: Replaces the nesting condition by a trivial-intersection condition; two distinct lines in the plane meet in $0$ but their union is not a subspace, and $U_1 = U_2 \neq 0$ gives a subspace with nonzero intersection.
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.

entries.input: Let $U, W$ be subspaces of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $V = U \oplus W$ (that is, $U$ and $W$ are complementary) if and only if $U + W = V$ and $U \cap W = 0$.
entries.name: DirectSumOfTwoIff
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (U W : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: IsCompl U W ↔ U ⊔ W = ⊤ ∧ U ⊓ W = ⊥
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0$, $W = V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: There exist subspaces $U_1, U_2, W$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $U_1 + W = U_2 + W$ but $U_1 \neq U_2$.
entries.name: SumOfSubspacesNotCancellative
entries.conclusion: ∃ U₁ U₂ W : Submodule ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ), U₁ ⊔ W = U₂ ⊔ W ∧ U₁ ≠ U₂
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is a closed existential.

entries.input: There exist subspaces $U_1, U_2, W$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\mathbb{R}^2 = U_1 \oplus W$ and $\mathbb{R}^2 = U_2 \oplus W$ but $U_1 \neq U_2$.
entries.name: ComplementNotUnique
entries.conclusion: ∃ U₁ U₂ W : Submodule ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ), IsCompl U₁ W ∧ IsCompl U₂ W ∧ U₁ ≠ U₂
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is a closed existential.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ and $S \subseteq V$. A vector $x$ lies in the span of $S$ if and only if $x$ is a finite linear combination $\sum_{i=1}^n c_i v_i$ of vectors $v_i \in S$.
entries.name: SpanEqLinearCombinations
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (S : Set V) (x : V)
entries.conclusion: x ∈ Submodule.span K S ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → K) (v : Fin n → V), (∀ i, v i ∈ S) ∧ x = ∑ i, c i • v i
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $S = \emptyset$ and $x = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $v_1, \dots, v_n$ be vectors in a vector space $V$ over a field $K$ (indexed by any type $\iota$). The family is linearly independent if and only if no $v_i$ lies in the span of the other $v_j$, $j \neq i$.
entries.name: LinearIndependentIffNotInSpanOfOthers
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {ι : Type*} (v : ι → V)
entries.conclusion: LinearIndependent K v ↔ ∀ i, v i ∉ Submodule.span K (v '' {i}ᶜ)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the empty family in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$. If $v_1, \dots, v_m$ are linearly independent and $w_1, \dots, w_n$ span $V$, then $m \le n$.
entries.name: IndependentLengthLeSpanningLength
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {m n : ℕ} (v : Fin m → V) (w : Fin n → V) (hv : LinearIndependent K v) (hw : Submodule.span K (Set.range w) = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: m ≤ n
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$, $m = 0$, $n = 1$, $w = (1)$.

entries.input: Every subspace $U$ of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$ is finite-dimensional.
entries.name: SubspaceOfFiniteDimensionalIsFiniteDimensional
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: FiniteDimensional K U
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $v_1, \dots, v_n$ be vectors in a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. They form a basis of $V$ (linearly independent and spanning) if and only if every $x \in V$ can be written in exactly one way as $x = a_1 v_1 + \dots + a_n v_n$ with $a_i \in K$.
entries.name: BasisIffUniqueRepresentation
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → V)
entries.conclusion: (LinearIndependent K v ∧ Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤) ↔ ∀ x : V, ∃! a : Fin n → K, x = ∑ i, a i • v i
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$, $n = 1$, $v = (1)$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ spanned by $w_1, \dots, w_n$. Then some subfamily $(w_i)_{i \in s}$ is a basis of $V$: it is linearly independent and still spans $V$.
entries.name: SpanningListContainsBasis
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → V) (hw : Submodule.span K (Set.range w) = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: ∃ s : Set (Fin n), LinearIndependent K (fun i : s => w i) ∧ Submodule.span K (w '' s) = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$, $w = (1)$.

entries.input: Every finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$ has a basis indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ for some $n$.
entries.name: FiniteDimensionalHasFiniteBasis
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V]
entries.conclusion: ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) K V)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Every vector space $V$ over a field $K$ has a basis: some subset $s \subseteq V$ is linearly independent and spans $V$.
entries.name: EveryVectorSpaceHasBasis
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
entries.conclusion: ∃ s : Set V, Nonempty (Module.Basis s K V)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$ and $v_1, \dots, v_m$ linearly independent vectors. Then there is a basis of $V$ containing every $v_i$: a set $s \supseteq \{v_1, \dots, v_m\}$ that is a basis of $V$.
entries.name: IndependentExtendsToBasis
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → V) (hv : LinearIndependent K v)
entries.conclusion: ∃ s : Set V, Set.range v ⊆ s ∧ ∃ b : Module.Basis s K V, ∀ x : s, b x = x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$, $m = 0$.

entries.input: Let $s$ be a subset of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $s$ is a basis of $V$ if and only if $s$ is linearly independent and no set strictly containing $s$ is linearly independent (that is, $s$ is a maximal linearly independent set).
entries.name: BasisIffMaximalIndependent
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (s : Set V)
entries.conclusion: (∃ b : Module.Basis s K V, ∀ x : s, b x = x) ↔ (LinearIndependent K ((↑) : s → V) ∧ ∀ t : Set V, s ⊂ t → ¬ LinearIndependent K ((↑) : t → V))
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $s = \{1\}$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $U$ be a subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $U$ has a complement: a subspace $W$ with $V = U \oplus W$.
entries.name: ComplementExists
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: ∃ W : Submodule K V, IsCompl U W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Any two bases of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$ that are indexed by $\{0,\dots,m-1\}$ and $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ have the same length: $m = n$.
entries.name: BasesHaveSameLength
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {m n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin m) K V) (c : Module.Basis (Fin n) K V)
entries.conclusion: m = n
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$ with $m = n = 1$ and $b = c = (1)$.

entries.input: Any two bases of a vector space $V$ over a field $K$, indexed by sets $\iota$ and $\kappa$, have the same cardinality: $|\iota| = |\kappa|$ as cardinal numbers. (No finiteness is assumed.)
entries.name: BasesHaveSameCardinality
entries.binders: {K : Type} [Field K] {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {ι κ : Type} (b : Module.Basis ι K V) (c : Module.Basis κ K V)
entries.conclusion: Cardinal.mk ι = Cardinal.mk κ
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$ with $\iota = \kappa$ a one-point type.

entries.input: If $U$ is a subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$, then $\dim U \le \dim V$.
entries.name: DimSubspaceLe
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K U ≤ Module.finrank K V
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $U$ be a subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$. If $\dim U = \dim V$, then $U = V$.
entries.name: SubspaceOfFullDimensionIsWhole
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U : Submodule K V) (h : Module.finrank K U = Module.finrank K V)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$ and $w_1, \dots, w_n$ a spanning list with $n = \dim V$. Then $w_1, \dots, w_n$ is linearly independent (hence a basis).
entries.name: SpanningOfLengthDimIsIndependent
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → V) (hw : Submodule.span K (Set.range w) = ⊤) (hn : n = Module.finrank K V)
entries.conclusion: LinearIndependent K w
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$, $n = 1$, $w = (1)$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$ and $v_1, \dots, v_n$ linearly independent with $n = \dim V$. Then $v_1, \dots, v_n$ spans $V$ (hence is a basis).
entries.name: IndependentOfLengthDimSpans
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → V) (hv : LinearIndependent K v) (hn : n = Module.finrank K V)
entries.conclusion: Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤

entries.input: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$ and $v_1, \dots, v_n$ linearly independent with $n + 1 = \dim V$. Then $v_1, \dots, v_n$ spans $V$.
entries.name: IndependentOfLengthDimSpansTwin
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → V) (hv : LinearIndependent K v) (hn : n + 1 = Module.finrank K V)
entries.conclusion: Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Shifts the length by one: $n$ independent vectors in an $(n+1)$-dimensional space never span.

entries.input: Let $U, W$ be subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $\dim(U + W) + \dim(U \cap W) = \dim U + \dim W$.
entries.name: DimSumAddDimInter
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U W : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K ↥(U ⊔ W) + Module.finrank K ↥(U ⊓ W) = Module.finrank K U + Module.finrank K W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = W = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $U, W$ be subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $\dim(U + W) = \dim U + \dim W$.
entries.name: DimSumAddDimInterTwin
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U W : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K ↥(U ⊔ W) = Module.finrank K U + Module.finrank K W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Drops the intersection term; it fails as soon as $U \cap W \neq 0$, for instance $U = W \neq 0$.

entries.input: Let $U_1, \dots, U_m$ be subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then $\dim(U_1 + \dots + U_m) \le \dim U_1 + \dots + \dim U_m$.
entries.name: DimSumLeSumDim
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] {m : ℕ} (U : Fin m → Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K ↥(⨆ i, U i) ≤ ∑ i, Module.finrank K ↥(U i)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $m = 0$ in $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $U, W$ be subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^8$ with $\dim U = 3$, $\dim W = 5$ and $U + W = \mathbb{R}^8$. Then $U \cap W = 0$.
entries.name: ThreePlusFiveInR8Disjoint
entries.binders: (U W : Submodule ℝ (Fin 8 → ℝ)) (hU : Module.finrank ℝ U = 3) (hW : Module.finrank ℝ W = 5) (h : U ⊔ W = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: U ⊓ W = ⊥
entries.witness_note: The binders are explicit, but a witness needs a concrete $3$-dimensional and $5$-dimensional pair with $U + W = \mathbb{R}^8$, whose dimension computations are not one-liners; the span of the first three and the last five coordinate vectors works.

entries.input: Let $U, W$ be $5$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^9$. Then $U \cap W \neq 0$.
entries.name: FiveFiveInR9Intersect
entries.binders: (U W : Submodule ℝ (Fin 9 → ℝ)) (hU : Module.finrank ℝ U = 5) (hW : Module.finrank ℝ W = 5)
entries.conclusion: U ⊓ W ≠ ⊥
entries.witness_note: The binders are explicit, but a witness needs a concrete pair of $5$-dimensional subspaces with the dimension computed; the span of the first five coordinate vectors, taken twice, works.

entries.input: A vector space $V$ over a field $K$ is infinite-dimensional if and only if there is a sequence $v_0, v_1, v_2, \dots$ in $V$ such that $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ is linearly independent for every $n$.
entries.name: InfiniteDimensionalIffIndependentSequence

entries.conclusion: ¬ FiniteDimensional K V ↔ ∃ v : ℕ → V, ∀ n : ℕ, LinearIndependent K (fun i : Fin n => v i)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: The real vector space of continuous real-valued functions on $[0, 1]$ is infinite-dimensional.
entries.name: ContinuousFunctionsInfiniteDimensional
entries.conclusion: ¬ FiniteDimensional ℝ (ContinuousMap (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) ℝ)
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: Let $K$ be a field and $p_0, \dots, p_m$ polynomials over $K$, each of degree at most $m$, with $p_j(2) = 0$ for every $j$. Then $p_0, \dots, p_m$ are linearly dependent.
entries.name: PolynomialsVanishingAtTwoDependent
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (p : Fin (m + 1) → Polynomial K) (hdeg : ∀ i, (p i).degree ≤ m) (h2 : ∀ i, (p i).eval 2 = 0)
entries.conclusion: ¬ LinearIndependent K p

entries.input: Let $v_1, \dots, v_n$ be linearly independent in a vector space $V$ over a field $K$ and $w \in V$. If $v_1 + w, \dots, v_n + w$ is linearly dependent, then $w \in \operatorname{span}(v_1, \dots, v_n)$.
entries.name: ShiftedDependentImpliesInSpan

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be vector spaces over a field $K$, $(b_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a basis of $V$ and $(w_i)_{i \in \iota}$ arbitrary vectors of $W$. Then there is exactly one linear map $T \colon V \to W$ with $T(b_i) = w_i$ for all $i$.

entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] {ι : Type*} (b : Module.Basis ι K V) (w : ι → W)
entries.conclusion: ∃! T : V →ₗ[K] W, ∀ i, T (b i) = w i

entries.input: A linear map $T \colon V \to W$ between vector spaces over a field $K$ is injective if and only if its null space is $\{0\}$.
entries.name: InjectiveIffKerTrivial
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective T ↔ LinearMap.ker T = ⊥

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$ with $V$ finite-dimensional. Then $\dim \ker T + \dim \operatorname{range} T = \dim V$.
entries.name: RankNullity
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker T) + Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range T) = Module.finrank K V
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = 0$ on $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$ with $V$ finite-dimensional. Then $\dim \ker T + \dim \operatorname{range} T = \dim W$.
entries.name: RankNullityTwin
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker T) + Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range T) = Module.finrank K W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Puts the dimension of the codomain on the right; the zero map $K \to K^2$ refutes it.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field $K$ with $\dim W < \dim V$. Then no linear map $V \to W$ is injective.
entries.name: NoInjectiveMapWhenDimDrops
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W) (h : Module.finrank K W < Module.finrank K V)
entries.conclusion: ¬ Function.Injective T
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = 0 \colon \mathbb{Q} \to 0$.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field $K$ with $\dim V < \dim W$. Then no linear map $V \to W$ is surjective.
entries.name: NoSurjectiveMapWhenDimRises
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W) (h : Module.finrank K V < Module.finrank K W)
entries.conclusion: ¬ Function.Surjective T

entries.input: Two finite-dimensional vector spaces $V, W$ over a field $K$ are isomorphic if and only if $\dim V = \dim W$.
entries.name: IsomorphicIffSameDim
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W]
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (V ≃ₗ[K] W) ↔ Module.finrank K V = Module.finrank K W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ with basis $(b_i)_{i \in \iota}$. Then $V$ is isomorphic to the space $K^{(\iota)}$ of finitely supported functions $\iota \to K$.
entries.name: SpaceIsoToFinitelySupportedFunctions
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {ι : Type*} (b : Module.Basis ι K V)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (V ≃ₗ[K] (ι →₀ K))
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = \mathbb{Q}$ with basis $(1)$.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field $K$. Then the space $\mathcal{L}(V, W)$ of linear maps is finite-dimensional of dimension $(\dim V)(\dim W)$.
entries.name: DimOfHomSpace
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W]
entries.conclusion: Module.finrank K (V →ₗ[K] W) = Module.finrank K V * Module.finrank K W
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be vector spaces over a field $K$ with bases $b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $V$ and $c_1, \dots, c_m$ of $W$. Sending a linear map $T$ to its $m \times n$ matrix, whose $(i, j)$ entry is the $c_i$-coordinate of $T(b_j)$, is a linear isomorphism $\mathcal{L}(V, W) \cong K^{m \times n}$.
entries.name: HomIsoMatrices
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] {m n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) K V) (c : Module.Basis (Fin m) K W)
entries.conclusion: ∃ e : (V →ₗ[K] W) ≃ₗ[K] Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) K, ∀ (T : V →ₗ[K] W) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n), e T i j = c.repr (T (b j)) i
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$ with the bases $(1)$.

entries.input: Let $U, V, W$ be vector spaces over a field $K$ with finite bases $b, c, d$ respectively, and $T \colon U \to V$, $S \colon V \to W$ linear. The matrix of $S \circ T$ with respect to $b, d$ is the product of the matrix of $S$ with respect to $c, d$ and the matrix of $T$ with respect to $b, c$.
entries.name: MatrixOfComposite
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {U V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module K U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] {l m n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin l) K U) (c : Module.Basis (Fin m) K V) (d : Module.Basis (Fin n) K W) (T : U →ₗ[K] V) (S : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: LinearMap.toMatrix b d (S ∘ₗ T) = LinearMap.toMatrix c d S * LinearMap.toMatrix b c T
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = V = W = \mathbb{Q}$ with the bases $(1)$ and $S = T = 0$.

entries.input: Every linear map $T \colon K^n \to K^m$ over a field $K$ is multiplication by a matrix: there is an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ with $T(x) = Ax$ for all $x$.
entries.name: LinearMapsOfCoordinateSpacesAreMatrices
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {m n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K))
entries.conclusion: ∃ A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) K, ∀ x, T x = A.mulVec x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = 0$ with $m = n = 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over a field $K$ and $\tau_A \colon K^n \to K^m$ the map $x \mapsto Ax$. Then $\tau_A$ is injective if and only if $\operatorname{rank} A = n$, and $\tau_A$ is surjective if and only if $\operatorname{rank} A = m$.
entries.name: MatrixMapInjectiveSurjectiveIffRank
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) K)
entries.conclusion: (Function.Injective (Matrix.mulVecLin A) ↔ A.rank = n) ∧ (Function.Surjective (Matrix.mulVecLin A) ↔ A.rank = m)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = (1)$ with $m = n = 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: For any $m \times n$ matrix $A$ over a field $K$, the row rank of $A$ equals its column rank: $\operatorname{rank} A^{\mathsf T} = \operatorname{rank} A$.
entries.name: RowRankEqColumnRank
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) K)
entries.conclusion: (Matrix.transpose A).rank = A.rank
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = 0$ with $m = n = 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to V$ be a linear operator on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$. Then $T$ is injective if and only if $T$ is surjective.
entries.name: EndoInjectiveIffSurjective
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (T : V →ₗ[K] V)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective T ↔ Function.Surjective T

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to V$ be a linear operator on a vector space over a field $K$. Then $T$ is injective if and only if $T$ is surjective.
entries.name: EndoInjectiveIffSurjectiveTwin
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (T : V →ₗ[K] V)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective T ↔ Function.Surjective T

entries.rationale: Drops finite-dimensionality; the right shift on $K^{\mathbb{N}}$ is injective and not surjective.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ with $\dim V = 1$ and $T \colon V \to V$ linear. Then there is $a \in K$ with $T v = a v$ for all $v \in V$.
entries.name: OneDimOperatorIsScalar
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (h : Module.finrank K V = 1) (T : V →ₗ[K] V)
entries.conclusion: ∃ a : K, ∀ v, T v = a • v
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = K = \mathbb{Q}$ with $T = \mathrm{id}$.

entries.input: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $K$, $U$ a subspace of $V$, $W$ a vector space over $K$ and $S \colon U \to W$ linear. Then $S$ extends to a linear map $T \colon V \to W$ with $T u = S u$ for all $u \in U$.

entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] (U : Submodule K V) (S : U →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: ∃ T : V →ₗ[K] W, ∀ u : U, T u = S u
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0 \le V = \mathbb{Q}$, $W = \mathbb{Q}$, $S = 0$.

entries.input: Let $f \colon V \to K$ be a linear functional on a vector space $V$ over a field $K$ and $u \in V$ with $f(u) \neq 0$. Then $V = \ker f \oplus K u$.
entries.name: FunctionalKernelComplementedByLine
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (f : V →ₗ[K] K) (u : V) (hu : f u ≠ 0)
entries.conclusion: IsCompl (LinearMap.ker f) (Submodule.span K {u})
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = K = \mathbb{Q}$, $f = \mathrm{id}$, $u = 1$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be an injective linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$. If $v_1, \dots, v_n$ are linearly independent in $V$, then $T v_1, \dots, T v_n$ are linearly independent in $W$.
entries.name: InjectivePreservesIndependence
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W) (hT : Function.Injective T) {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → V) (hv : LinearIndependent K v)
entries.conclusion: LinearIndependent K (T ∘ v)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = \mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ with $n = 0$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$. Then $T$ is injective if and only if $T$ carries every linearly independent subset of $V$ to a linearly independent family in $W$.
entries.name: InjectiveIffPreservesIndependence
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective T ↔ ∀ s : Set V, LinearIndependent K ((↑) : s → V) → LinearIndependent K (fun x : s => T x)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = \mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $S_1, \dots, S_n$ be injective linear operators on a vector space $V$ over a field $K$. Then the composite $S_1 \circ \dots \circ S_n$ is injective.
entries.name: CompositeOfInjectiveIsInjective
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {n : ℕ} (S : Fin n → V →ₗ[K] V) (hS : ∀ i, Function.Injective (S i))
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective ((List.ofFn S).prod)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $n = 0$ on $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a surjective linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$. If $w_1, \dots, w_n$ span $V$, then $T w_1, \dots, T w_n$ span $W$.
entries.name: SurjectivePreservesSpanning
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W) (hT : Function.Surjective T) {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → V) (hw : Submodule.span K (Set.range w) = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: Submodule.span K (Set.range (T ∘ w)) = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = \mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ with $w = (1)$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$ with $V$ finite-dimensional. Then there is a subspace $U$ of $V$ with $U \cap \ker T = 0$ and $T(U) = \operatorname{range} T$.
entries.name: RangeFromComplementOfKernel
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: ∃ U : Submodule K V, U ⊓ LinearMap.ker T = ⊥ ∧ U.map T = LinearMap.range T
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = 0$ on $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $K$ be a field and $T \colon K^4 \to K^2$ a linear map whose null space is $\{(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4) : x_1 = 5 x_2,\ x_3 = 7 x_4\}$. Then $T$ is surjective.
entries.name: F4ToF2WithGivenKernelSurjective
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] (T : (Fin 4 → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin 2 → K)) (h : (LinearMap.ker T : Set (Fin 4 → K)) = {x | x 0 = 5 * x 1 ∧ x 2 = 7 * x 3})
entries.conclusion: Function.Surjective T

entries.input: Let $K$ be a field. There is no linear map $T \colon K^5 \to K^2$ whose null space is $\{(x_1, \dots, x_5) : x_1 = 3 x_2,\ x_3 = x_4 = x_5\}$.
entries.name: NoF5ToF2WithGivenKernel
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K]
entries.conclusion: ¬ ∃ T : (Fin 5 → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin 2 → K), (LinearMap.ker T : Set (Fin 5 → K)) = {x | x 0 = 3 * x 1 ∧ x 2 = x 3 ∧ x 3 = x 4}
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $K = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to V$ be a linear operator on a vector space over a field $K$. If both $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{range} T$ are finite-dimensional, then $V$ is finite-dimensional.
entries.name: FiniteKernelAndRangeImpliesFiniteDimensional
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (T : V →ₗ[K] V) [FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.ker T)] [FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.range T)]
entries.conclusion: FiniteDimensional K V
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = 0$ on $V = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field $K$. There is a surjective linear map $V \to W$ if and only if $\dim W \le \dim V$.
entries.name: SurjectiveExistsIffDimLe
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W]
entries.conclusion: (∃ T : V →ₗ[K] W, Function.Surjective T) ↔ Module.finrank K W ≤ Module.finrank K V
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $V, W$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field $K$ and $U$ a subspace of $V$. There is a linear map $T \colon V \to W$ with $\ker T = U$ if and only if $\dim U \ge \dim V - \dim W$ (with truncated subtraction: the condition is automatic when $\dim W \ge \dim V$).
entries.name: KernelPrescribedIffDim
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W] (U : Submodule K V)
entries.conclusion: (∃ T : V →ₗ[K] W, LinearMap.ker T = U) ↔ Module.finrank K V - Module.finrank K W ≤ Module.finrank K U
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $U = 0 \le V = W = \mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$ with $W$ finite-dimensional. Then $T$ is injective if and only if there is a linear map $S \colon W \to V$ with $S \circ T = \mathrm{id}_V$.
entries.name: InjectiveIffLeftInverse
entries.binders: {K : Type*} [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K W] (T : V →ₗ[K] W)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective T ↔ ∃ S : W →ₗ[K] V, S ∘ₗ T = LinearMap.id
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a field, a space or an operator type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $T = \mathrm{id}$ on $\mathbb{Q}$.

entries.input: Let $T \colon V \to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over a field $K$ with $V$ finite-dimensional. Then $T$ is surjective if and only if there is a linear map $S \colon W \to V$ with $T \circ S = \mathrm{id}_W$.
entries.name: SurjectiveIffRightInverse

entries.input: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix over an algebraically closed field $K$. Then $\operatorname{tr} A$ is the sum of the roots of the characteristic polynomial of $A$ (the eigenvalues, with multiplicity), and $\det A$ is their product.

entries.input: Let $n \geq 2$ and let $A = [a_{i,j}]_{i,j=1}^{n}$ be a matrix of nonnegative integers with $a_{i,j} = 0$ whenever $i + j \leq n$, with $a_{i+1,j} \in \{a_{i,j}, a_{i,j}+1\}$ for $i < n$, and with $a_{i,j+1} \in \{a_{i,j}, a_{i,j}+1\}$ for $j < n$.
